strengths: Introduces a novel guided decoding framework that decouples positional guidance (target-aware queries) from content representation (key-value pairs), enabling random-order autoregressive image generation with causal attention and KV caching.

Enables efficient parallel decoding via shared KV cache and batched queries, delivering substantial throughput and memory improvements over representative autoregressive baselines such as LlamaGen, VAR, and RandAR.
Achieves strong class-conditional generation on ImageNet-1K 256x256, reaching FID 1.94 with only 64 sampling steps and IS 339.7, while outperforming recent random-order AR methods like RandAR.
Demonstrates applicability to controllable generation with Canny edges and depth maps, outperforming ControlVAR and ControlAR on those tasks.
Provides useful ablations on decoder design, shared KV, generation order, and efficiency-quality trade-offs, supporting the main design choices.
Supports zero-shot generalization qualitatively for inpainting, outpainting, class-conditional editing, and resolution expansion, illustrating the flexibility of randomized generation.
The paper is generally well written, with clear diagrams, pseudo-code, and supplementary implementation details.
weaknesses: Zero-shot generalization claims (inpainting, outpainting, resolution expansion) are evaluated only qualitatively; no quantitative metrics, baselines, or user studies are provided despite these being emphasized as key advantages.

Parallel decoding of multiple queries in one step assumes independence among simultaneously generated tokens, which is an approximation to the exact autoregressive factorization; the paper does not theoretically or empirically analyze this approximation's effect on sample quality or likelihood.

The derivation supporting the removal of unmasked queries (Insight 2) contains questionable/inconsistent steps, and the causal mask notation in Eq. (11) (i <= j) appears reversed relative to standard causal attention, weakening the theoretical presentation.

Throughput claims such as 'over 20-fold' are sensitive to sampling steps and baseline choice; at 64 steps and comparable scales, speedups over LlamaGen are closer to 14-16x, and memory reduction claims are not uniformly above 75% across all cited baselines.
Reproducibility is limited: no code or checkpoints are released, and details about training compute, exact zero-shot evaluation settings, and permutation sampling at inference are incomplete.
Controllable generation results are restricted to two conditions (Canny and depth) and a single model scale, without extension to text-to-image or broader conditional modalities.
The 512x512 evaluation is limited to a fine-tuned model with only 50 epochs, and its FID (3.38) is not state-of-the-art compared with some diffusion/VAR baselines.
Some baseline categorization is confusing, e.g., RAR is labeled as 'AR (Raster)' although it is commonly considered a randomized autoregressive method, which may make comparisons harder to interpret.

strengths: Introduces a simple and effective decoupling of positional guidance (queries) and content representation (keys/values) in causal attention, enabling random-order training and parallel decoding while retaining KV-cache compatibility.

Achieves strong efficiency improvements: high throughput (e.g., 113 it/s at 32 steps for ARPG-L) and low memory (2.43 GB at 64 steps), with competitive FID (2.44/2.10/1.94 at L/XL/XXL scales on ImageNet-1K 256x256).
Extensive experiments include class-conditional generation on 256x256 and 512x512, controllable generation with Canny/depth conditions, ablations on decoder design, shared KV, and generation order.
The method naturally supports controllable and zero-shot tasks such as inpainting, outpainting, class-conditional editing, and resolution expansion without architectural changes.
weaknesses: The parallel decoding is not exact autoregressive sampling: multiple tokens predicted in one step are treated as conditionally independent given the same context, violating the sequential factorization in Eq. (8). The paper does not quantify the approximation error or compare against exact sequential sampling in the same random order.

Zero-shot generalization claims (inpainting, outpainting, resolution expansion) are only qualitatively demonstrated. No quantitative metrics (e.g., FID, IS, PSNR, SSIM) are provided for these tasks, so the central claim of robust zero-shot generalization is unsupported.

Novelty is incremental over RandAR and other random-order AR methods. The proposed 'guided decoding' mainly moves positional instruction tokens into query embeddings; the theoretical 'insights' are either trivial (gradients of unmasked queries) or stated as an assumption rather than proved.

The paper overstates its quality claims. On ImageNet 256x256, RAR (raster-order) achieves better FID (1.50 at 955M) than ARPG-XXL (1.94 at 1.3B), contradicting the claim of surpassing raster-order baselines. ARPG is only better than RandAR, a narrower comparison.

Mathematical formulation has off-by-one inconsistencies (e.g., p(x)=∏_{i=1}^n p(x_{τ_{i+1}}|...)), and the proof in Insight 2 does not justify Insight 3, which is presented as an assumption. This weakens technical soundness.

Evaluation is limited to ImageNet class-conditional and small-scale controllable generation; no text-to-image experiments or comparison to recent diffusion/consistency models under matched compute. Reproducibility is limited by missing training compute details and pseudo-code errors.

The two-pass decoder architecture is not sufficiently analyzed: it doubles depth in some sense, and efficiency benefits rely heavily on shared KV and batch-size-specific throughput measurements. The architectural trade-offs are not theoretically motivated.

strengths: Introduces a novel guided decoding framework that decouples target-aware positional queries from data-dependent key-value pairs, enabling random-order autoregressive training and parallel decoding with causal attention and KV cache, avoiding the need for bidirectional attention or extra instruction tokens.

Provides a principled reformulation of permuted autoregressive modeling (Eq. 8) with theoretical insights, including a gradient-based justification for removing unmasked tokens from queries and [MASK] tokens from key-value pairs.

Achieves strong empirical results on ImageNet-1K 256x256 and 512x512: competitive FID (1.94 at XXL with 64 steps), substantially higher throughput and lower memory than representative AR models such as LlamaGen and VAR, and state-of-the-art performance among random-order causal models like RandAR.
Includes thorough ablations on decoder design, shared KV, sampling steps, and generation order, which support the design choices and demonstrate the efficiency-quality trade-off.

Extends the method to controllable generation with canny/depth conditions and qualitatively demonstrates zero-shot inpainting, outpainting, class-conditional editing, and resolution expansion, with supplementary pseudo-code aiding reproducibility.
weaknesses: Parallel decoding assumes conditional independence among tokens generated in the same step, but training uses causal dependencies within the shuffled random order; the approximation and its effect on sample quality are not theoretically analyzed or ablated.
Zero-shot generalization tasks (inpainting, outpainting, resolution expansion) are shown only qualitatively; no quantitative metrics or comparisons are provided for these central claims.

The abstract's claim of 'over 20-fold' throughput improvement is not consistently supported by Table 2 at 64 sampling steps (e.g., ~14-16x versus LlamaGen models); the FID of 1.94 is also not the best among all compared AR baselines (e.g., RAR-XL reports 1.50).

Scope is limited to class-conditional ImageNet and controllable/depth/canny generation; text-to-image and larger-scale validation are absent, which the authors acknowledge but which still limits impact.
A few technical/typographical issues remain, such as the causal mask definition in Eq. 11 and omitted details of RoPE shifting and KV-cache updates in the main paper/pseudocode.

strengths: Proposes a novel decoupled two-pass decoder that separates positional guidance from content representation, enabling random-order training and parallel decoding with causal attention and KV cache reuse.

Achieves strong efficiency gains: over 30x speedup and ~75% memory reduction compared with LlamaGen-style autoregressive models at similar scale, while attaining competitive ImageNet-1K 256x256 FID (e.g., 1.83 with 32 steps).

Extensive and convincing experiments: class-conditional generation, text-to-image, controllable generation, zero-shot qualitative tasks, and ablations over architecture, attention pattern, decoding steps, positional encodings, and generation orders.

Provides useful empirical and architectural insights, including the redundancy of attending to [MASK] tokens in coupled random-order models and the benefits of decoupling queries from key-value representations.
Supports flexible zero-shot inference such as inpainting, outpainting, and resolution expansion without task-specific fine-tuning, which is a desirable property for visual autoregressive models.
weaknesses: Zero-shot generalization claims are only supported qualitatively; there are no quantitative metrics for inpainting, outpainting, or resolution expansion, weakening one of the paper's stated contributions.
The theoretical proof in Appendix C is informal and arguably incorrect in its attention-gradient derivation; it does not rigorously establish the claimed training inefficiency of masked modeling.
The claim that the method 'surpasses raster-order baselines' needs qualification: RAR-XL achieves a better FID (1.50) than ARPG-XXL (1.83), even though ARPG is much faster and more memory efficient.

The headline speed/memory comparison is primarily against LlamaGen; against stronger/faster baselines such as RAR, the speedup and memory reduction are considerably smaller, and Fig. 1(b) omits some relevant baselines.

Some reproducibility and clarity issues remain: exact Pass-2 causal masking, block-wise attention generalization details, training compute, and code are not fully specified; there are also citation/attribution errors and typos.
No limitations or broader societal impact discussion is provided, despite the paper dealing with image generation technology.

strengths: Proposes ARPG, a two-pass decoder that decouples positional guidance from content representation: Pass-1 builds causal KV representations from known tokens, while Pass-2 uses data-independent [MASK] queries with RoPE positional information as target-aware queries. This enables random-order autoregressive generation without doubling sequence length as in RandAR.

Achieves strong class-conditional ImageNet 256x256 results: FID of 1.83, 1.93, and 2.30 at 32 sampling steps for XXL/XL/L models, with high throughput (55-130 img/s) and low memory (2.78-7.22 GB), often providing a better quality-efficiency trade-off than VAR, LlamaGen, PAR, NAR, and RandAR.

Supports flexible-order and parallel decoding, and qualitatively demonstrates zero-shot inpainting, outpainting, editing, and resolution expansion, as well as controllable generation with competitive FID against ControlAR/ControlVAR.

Includes useful ablations on architecture design (Pass-1/Pass-2 layer ratio, shared KV projection, positional encoding), attention pattern (causal vs. block-wise), sampling steps, sampling orders, and model scalability.
Provides PyTorch-style pseudo-code and detailed hyperparameter configurations, which aids partial reproducibility.
The idea of using positional queries to attend to content KV pairs is conceptually clean and leads to practical efficiency gains.
weaknesses: Novelty is incremental over RandAR, XLNet-style permutation modeling, and masked autoregressive approaches. The decoupled query-KV design is a reasonable architectural improvement, but the paper overstates its distinctiveness and does not provide a fundamental advance.

Zero-shot generalization claims are only qualitatively demonstrated. There is no quantitative evaluation on inpainting, outpainting, editing, or resolution expansion, no comparison to task-specific or zero-shot baselines, and insufficient details on sampling schedules/CFG for these tasks.

Text-to-image performance is not competitive with diffusion models: GenEval overall is 0.31 for ARPG-XL vs. 0.43 for SD-v1.5 and 0.39 for Chameleon. The claim of high-quality text-to-image generation is therefore overstated, especially given the limited data and baselines.

The theoretical justification for Insight 2 is trivial: it only shows that queries for unmasked tokens receive zero direct gradient in standard softmax attention. It does not prove masked modeling is inherently inefficient or that ARPG fully avoids the issue.

The claim that generalizing from causal to block-wise attention at inference does not compromise the probabilistic model is unsupported. Training uses causal attention, while inference uses block-wise/bidirectional attention among previously generated tokens, changing the conditional distributions. The FID improvements in Table 8 do not establish probabilistic correctness.

Efficiency claims may be cherry-picked. The 30x speedup is against LlamaGen-L, which uses 576 steps; against VAR-d16 the throughput gain is minimal (130 vs. 123 img/s). Profiling only the token generation process may overstate end-to-end practical gains.
Reproducibility is limited by no code release and incomplete zero-shot evaluation details. There is no discussion of limitations, failure cases, or broader societal impact.

There are some citation/table errors, e.g., NAR is attributed to Wang et al. 2025 rather than He et al. 2025, and the claim that 64 steps gives the best visual quality is contradicted by the reported FID/IS trends.

strengths: Introduces a novel decoupled two-pass decoding architecture for autoregressive image generation, where positional guidance is separated from content representation via [MASK]-based queries and KV pairs from a causal content decoder.
Enables fully random-order training while retaining causal attention, and supports parallel decoding by processing multiple target-aware queries in a single step with a shared KV cache.

Strong efficiency results: ARPG-XXL achieves FID 1.83 on ImageNet-1K 256x256 with 32 sampling steps, over 30x higher throughput and 75% lower memory than recent autoregressive baselines such as LlamaGen and VAR.
Broad applicability demonstrated across class-conditional generation, text-to-image generation, controllable generation, inpainting, outpainting, and resolution expansion.
Ablation studies analyze decoding steps, attention pattern generalization, architecture design, positional encoding, and sampling order, providing useful insights into the proposed design.
Implementation details and pseudo-code are provided, supporting reproducibility of the core method and training/inference pipeline.
weaknesses: Zero-shot generalization claims (inpainting, outpainting, resolution expansion) are supported only qualitatively; no quantitative evaluation or comparison is provided for these tasks.

Text-to-image generation results are not state-of-the-art: GenEval overall score 0.31 is comparable to LlamaGen but below SD-v1.5 (0.43), and the evaluation uses a relatively small 4M-image subset, limiting conclusions about scaling.
Controllable generation improvements over ControlAR are modest (e.g., Canny FID 7.39 vs. 7.69, Depth 4.06 vs. 4.19), and comparisons are limited to a small set of baselines.

The claim of eliminating bidirectional attention is somewhat overstated because inference generalizes to block-wise attention, which is locally bidirectional within generated blocks; the paper does not fully reconcile this with the causal training formulation.

The theoretical proof in Appendix C mainly addresses the final-layer query gradient for unmasked tokens; the claimed training inefficiency of masked modeling relies on indirect-gradient arguments that are not fully formalized.
Novelty overlaps with prior random-order/parallel decoding work such as RandAR and XLNet; the main distinction is efficiency-oriented decoupling rather than a fundamentally new modeling paradigm.
No quantitative comparison on downstream tasks such as inpainting/outpainting and no discussion of ethical risks or misuse of high-fidelity image generation.
